answer: No adjuvant therapy is indicated; continue monitoring with PSA surveillance because the pathology has no adverse features and no nodal involvement.

Observation (monitoring without surveillance biopsies or PSA-driven treatment, with symptom-directed intervention if needed) is recommended because he is asymptomatic with life expectancy under 10 years.

He meets the Phoenix definition of biochemical recurrence after EBRT (PSA at least 2 ng/mL above nadir), so start the recurrence workup: PSADT calculation, bone and soft tissue imaging, and consideration of prostate biopsy, then choose local or systemic therapy based on the results.
Given persistent PSA without M1 disease on PSMA PET, offer secondary EBRT to the prostate bed (with or without ADT), since early secondary treatment at PSA 0.1 to 0.2 ng/mL is recommended.
Observation is recommended: he is asymptomatic with life expectancy about 3 years, so monitor PSA and imaging for symptoms or rising PSA rather than treat now.
Oligorecurrent M1 disease detected on PET (two pelvic bone lesions, no visceral disease) is treated with metastasis-directed radiation therapy alone or with short-term ADT (about 6 months).

Metastatic castration-sensitive disease with high-volume visceral (liver) involvement calls for ADT plus treatment intensification: ADT with docetaxel and an ARPI (triplet, preferred if fit for chemotherapy) or ADT plus an ARPI (doublet, also suitable).

Confirmatory biopsy showing Grade Group 3 means he is no longer a candidate for active surveillance; transition to definitive treatment (radical prostatectomy or radiation therapy, with or without ADT) through shared decision-making, given his 25-year life expectancy.
